    def test_prepared_request_is_pickleable(self, httpbin):
        p = requests.Request("GET", httpbin("get")).prepare()

        # Verify PreparedRequest can be pickled and unpickled
        r = pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(p))
        assert r.url == p.url
        assert r.headers == p.headers
        assert r.body == p.body

        # Verify unpickled PreparedRequest sends properly
        s = requests.Session()
        resp = s.send(r)
        assert resp.status_code == 200

    def test_prepared_request_with_file_is_pickleable(self, httpbin):
        with open(__file__, "rb") as f:
            r = requests.Request("POST", httpbin("post"), files={"file": f})
            p = r.prepare()

        # Verify PreparedRequest can be pickled and unpickled
        r = pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(p))
        assert r.url == p.url
        assert r.headers == p.headers
        assert r.body == p.body

        # Verify unpickled PreparedRequest sends properly
        s = requests.Session()
        resp = s.send(r)
        assert resp.status_code == 200

    def test_prepared_request_with_hook_is_pickleable(self, httpbin):
        r = requests.Request("GET", httpbin("get"), hooks=default_hooks())

        # Verify PreparedRequest can be pickled
        r = pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(p))
        assert r.url == p.url
        assert r.headers == p.headers
        assert r.body == p.body
        assert r.hooks == p.hooks

        # Verify unpickled PreparedRequest sends properly
        s = requests.Session()
        resp = s.send(r)
        assert resp.status_code == 200

BASEADAPTER, also known as `BaseAdapter`, is an abstract transport adapter class used by the Requests library. It defines the fundamental operations required for transport adapters, including certificate verification and closing connections. The class is intended to be subclassed when implementing custom Requests transport adapters. Because it provides an interface rather than a complete implementation, some of its methods may raise `NotImplementedError` until they are overridden by a concrete subclass.

Requests adapters are the transport-level components of the Requests module responsible for handling HTTP requests and managing HTTP transport behavior. The `requests.adapters` module defines the `HTTPAdapter`, which provides the adapter implementation used to connect Requests with HTTP transport mechanisms and is also used by the test suite.

HTTPADAPTER is the built-in Requests transport adapter for HTTP and HTTPS URLs. It is mounted on URL prefixes, typically through a Requests session, to deliver requests through the underlying urllib3 transport layer. HTTPADAPTER creates and manages connection pools and urllib3 connections, supports proxy managers, applies TLS and SSL certificate verification settings, and provides standard request-related connection methods. It also manages serialization state and adapter-specific cleanup. As the default adapter for HTTP and HTTPS, HTTPADAPTER can be configured with retry behavior, including retry-enabled handling for HTTPS requests, and can be extended for custom SSL or other connection settings.

SESSION is a Requests library client object that manages persistent state and configuration while sending multiple HTTP and HTTPS requests. It stores and applies cookies, headers, authentication, proxy settings, hooks, environment settings, certificates, and TLS verification options. SESSION creates and mounts HTTPAdapter instances to contact HTTP and HTTPS URLs, maintaining separate connection pools when TLS configurations differ and providing connection pooling for efficient reuse. It prepares and sends requests, including prepared requests, resolves redirect chains subject to configured redirect limits, and manages the adapters used for network communication. SESSION also supports pickling and serves as the central mechanism for maintaining consistent request behavior across a series of HTTP operations.

RETRY is the urllib3 utility class used by Requests to configure automatic retry behavior through an HTTPAdapter. It controls the number of retry attempts for failures such as DNS lookup errors, socket connection failures, and connection timeouts. RETRY also defines backoff behavior, status-based retry conditions, and the HTTP methods eligible for retrying.

BASEADAPTER, also known as `BaseAdapter`, is an abstract transport adapter class used by the Requests library. It defines the fundamental operations required for transport adapters, including certificate verification and closing connections. The class is intended to be subclassed when implementing custom Requests transport adapters. Because it provides an interface rather than a complete implementation, some of its methods may raise `NotImplementedError` until they are overridden by a concrete subclass.

Requests adapters are the transport-level components of the Requests module responsible for handling HTTP requests and managing HTTP transport behavior. The `requests.adapters` module defines the `HTTPAdapter`, which provides the adapter implementation used to connect Requests with HTTP transport mechanisms and is also used by the test suite.

HTTPADAPTER is the built-in Requests transport adapter for HTTP and HTTPS URLs. It is mounted on URL prefixes, typically through a Requests session, to deliver requests through the underlying urllib3 transport layer. HTTPADAPTER creates and manages connection pools and urllib3 connections, supports proxy managers, applies TLS and SSL certificate verification settings, and provides standard request-related connection methods. It also manages serialization state and adapter-specific cleanup. As the default adapter for HTTP and HTTPS, HTTPADAPTER can be configured with retry behavior, including retry-enabled handling for HTTPS requests, and can be extended for custom SSL or other connection settings.

SESSION is a Requests library client object that manages persistent state and configuration while sending multiple HTTP and HTTPS requests. It stores and applies cookies, headers, authentication, proxy settings, hooks, environment settings, certificates, and TLS verification options. SESSION creates and mounts HTTPAdapter instances to contact HTTP and HTTPS URLs, maintaining separate connection pools when TLS configurations differ and providing connection pooling for efficient reuse. It prepares and sends requests, including prepared requests, resolves redirect chains subject to configured redirect limits, and manages the adapters used for network communication. SESSION also supports pickling and serves as the central mechanism for maintaining consistent request behavior across a series of HTTP operations.

RETRY is the urllib3 utility class used by Requests to configure automatic retry behavior through an HTTPAdapter. It controls the number of retry attempts for failures such as DNS lookup errors, socket connection failures, and connection timeouts. RETRY also defines backoff behavior, status-based retry conditions, and the HTTP methods eligible for retrying.
